caption:
You can tell what a garment is worth before you look at the label. Four checks, about ten seconds, and they work in any shop at any price.

Save it for the next time you're out.
caption_fb: You can tell what a garment is worth before you look at the label. Four checks, about ten seconds, at any price point.
first_comment: The seam allowance is the one nobody checks — and it's the one that decides whether it survives being taken in.

slides.headline: Judge it before you see the price.
slides.subhead: Four checks, ten seconds. They work in a charity shop and they work at full price.
slides.alt: Cover: judge a garment before you see the price

slides.headline: Turn it inside out first
slides.body: The outside is styled. The inside is *built*. Finished seams, bound edges and clean overlocking are where the money actually went.
slides.alt: Turn the garment inside out to see construction

slides.headline: Seam allowance is the tell
slides.body: A generous allowance means it can be let out or taken in. A narrow one means the fabric was rationed and the fit is final.
slides.alt: A 1.5cm seam allowance indicates quality construction

slides.headline: Follow the pattern across a seam
slides.body: On a stripe or check, matched lines across the join take extra fabric and extra care. A broken pattern is a shortcut you can *see*.
slides.alt: Check whether patterns match across seams

slides.headline: The four checks
items: Inside out — are the seams finished?
Seam allowance — is there room to alter?
Pattern — does it match at the join?
Hold it to the light — can you see through it?
slides.alt: Four quality checks listed in order

slides.quote: Fabric weight is the one thing a photograph can never tell you.
slides.alt: Pull quote about fabric weight and photographs

slides.headline: Buy less, check harder
slides.body: Food and fashion, three breakdowns a week. No hauls, no affiliate links.
